sample_unit: GPT-4 generated outputs (vignettes, differential diagnoses, treatment plans) across demographic variations

links.outcome: Change in GPT-4 diagnoses and plans when patient race/ethnicity/gender varied in standardized vignettes
links.effect: Differential diagnoses were more likely to include stereotyping diagnoses; plans showed significant association between demographics and recommendations for more expensive procedures and differences in patient perception.
links.quote: Assessment and plans created by the model showed significant association between demographic attributes and recommendations for more expensive procedures as well as differences in patient perception.

links.outcome: Stereotyping and demographic misrepresentation in GPT-4 generated clinical vignettes
links.effect: GPT-4 did not appropriately model the demographic diversity of medical conditions, consistently producing vignettes that stereotype demographic presentations, compared with true U.S. prevalence.
links.quote: We find that GPT-4 does not appropriately model the demographic diversity of medical conditions, consistently producing clinical vignettes that stereotype demographic presentations.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of demographic and racial/gender bias in GPT-4 using clinical vignettes across diagnostic reasoning and treatment planning, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice intervention.
